packages.name: Core
packages.description: The base every ArchNet service plugs into: bootstrap, Services.Get<T>(), event bus, safe JSON files and UI panels.

packages.name: Facade Pattern
packages.description: Learning package: a sample showing the Facade pattern, one simple entry point to several systems.

packages.name: Factory Pattern
packages.description: Creates objects from a key without the calling code knowing their concrete type: Factory<TKey, TProduct>.

packages.name: Object Pooling Pattern
packages.description: Reuses copies of a prefab instead of creating and destroying them, built on Unity's ObjectPool.

packages.name: Singleton Pattern
packages.description: A MonoBehaviour that exists once in the scene, reachable from anywhere with MyManager.Instance.

packages.name: Singleton ScriptableObject Pattern
packages.description: One shared ScriptableObject asset (settings, databases…) reachable from anywhere with MySettings.Instance, in builds too.

packages.name: Canvas Extension
packages.description: Responsive UI for phones, tablets and computers (Safe Area, Responsive Canvas, Responsive Switch), plus extension methods for Canvas and CanvasGroup.

packages.name: Color Extension
packages.description: Colors a UI element or a SpriteRenderer from a Color Library key, so the palette lives in one asset.

packages.name: Dictionary Extension
packages.description: Extension methods for dictionaries: copy a dictionary without its empty values.

packages.name: Dont Destroy On Load Extension
packages.description: Add this component to keep its GameObject alive when a new scene loads (managers, music player…).

packages.name: Dropzone Extension
packages.description: Fills a container (layout group, list…) with copies of prefabs and removes them when the container is disabled.

packages.name: Load Scene Extension
packages.description: Scenes of your game: a loading screen with progress and tips, a ready main menu and a gameplay scene with a pause menu. The ModuleScenes component is still there.

packages.name: Renderer Extension
packages.description: Tells whether a screen point, or objects of the scene, are inside a UI rectangle, for every canvas mode.

packages.name: Reverse Mask 2D Extension
packages.description: Darkens the whole UI with an overlay except the elements you highlight, which are drawn above it (tutorials).

packages.name: Reverse Mask 3D Extension
packages.description: Darkens the screen with an overlay that has holes over 3D objects; clicks inside a hole reach the object under it.

packages.name: Rotation Extension
packages.description: Spins its GameObject around an axis at a set speed (loading icons, coins, fans…).

packages.name: ScriptableObject Extension
packages.description: Helpers for assets: get the file name of a ScriptableObject (or any asset), in the Editor and in builds.

packages.name: ScrollRect Extension
packages.description: Extension methods for scroll views: jump to an edge, lock scrolling, tell a horizontal drag from a vertical one.

packages.name: Sprite Extension
packages.description: Shows a sprite from an Image Library key on a UI Image or a SpriteRenderer, so icons are picked by name.

packages.name: Audio Library
packages.description: Audio clips stored by enum or int key, so code plays sounds by name and a clip can be replaced in one place.

packages.name: Color Library
packages.description: Your game's palette in one asset: colors stored by enum or int key, so changing a color updates every place that uses it.

packages.name: Image Library
packages.description: Links each sprite of a Sprite Atlas to an enum value or an int, so code asks for Icon.Sword instead of a sprite name that can change.

packages.name: Library Core
packages.description: Base of the ArchNet libraries: a ScriptableObject that stores values by int or enum key, with one shared inspector. Derive from KeyedLibrary<T> to make your own library.

packages.name: Material Library
packages.description: Materials stored by enum or int key, so code swaps materials by name instead of holding references everywhere.

packages.name: Prefab Library
packages.description: Prefabs stored by enum or int key and spawned by key, so spawners and level data never hold prefab references directly.

packages.name: Audio Module
packages.description: Deprecated: use the Settings Module, which has volumes per channel. Audio settings for an options menu: volume and mute for music and game sounds.

packages.name: Credit Module
packages.description: A scrolling credits screen built from a list of names you edit in a window, opened from anywhere with Services.Get<GameCredits>().Play().

packages.name: Localization Module
packages.description: Your game in several languages: JSON files per language, labels that follow the language, a language dropdown, and a key editor with CSV import / export.

packages.name: Runtime Module
packages.description: A debug panel for builds: press F1 to show live data (FPS, audio, graphics, screen, platform, version…).

packages.name: Shadow Module
packages.description: Deprecated: it changes the QualitySettings shadows, which URP ignores; use the Settings Module. Shadow settings for an options menu (type and resolution).

packages.name: Video Module
packages.description: Deprecated: use the Settings Module, which covers it. Video settings for an options menu: resolution, window mode, quality level and anti-aliasing.

packages.name: Console Service
packages.description: A second console for your own messages, sorted by priority and shown in its own window, each with its call stack.

packages.name: Popup Service
packages.description: Alerts, yes / no questions and text prompts you await from code, one at a time.

packages.name: Local Save Module
packages.description: Save slots for your game data as JSON files on the device, with autosave and upgrades of old saves.

packages.name: Data Service
packages.description: Your game data (items, enemies, levels…) as JSON tables, read with typed classes.

packages.name: Settings Module
packages.description: A complete options menu (general, audio, video), applied at once and saved. Replaces the Audio, Video and Shadow modules.

packages.name: Input Module
packages.description: Keyboard, mouse and gamepad controls on the Input System, the Escape / Back key that closes menus and pauses, and a screen to change keys.

packages.name: Notification Service
packages.description: In-game notifications (info, success, warning, error) in a corner of the screen, a few at a time.

packages.name: API Service
packages.description: Web API calls in one line (Get, Post, Put, Delete), JSON, environments, timeout, retries, clear errors.

services.name: ArchNet Bootstrap
services.description: Starts your game services once, before the first scene, and keeps them alive between scenes. Every other service plugs into it.

services.name: Credits
services.description: A scrolling credits screen built from your list of names, and a window to edit them. Open it from anywhere: Services.Get<GameCredits>().Play().

services.name: Popups
services.description: Alerts, yes / no questions and text prompts you await from code, one at a time: await Services.Get<GamePopups>().Confirm("Quit", "Leave the game?").

services.name: Save
services.description: Save slots for your game data on the device, with autosave and upgrades of old saves: Services.Get<GameSave>().Save().

services.name: Data
services.description: Your game data (items, enemies, levels…) as JSON tables edited in a window, read with typed classes: Services.Get<GameData>().Items.

services.name: Settings
services.description: A complete options menu (general, audio, video) applied at once and saved: frame rate, V-Sync, volumes, display, resolution, quality.

services.name: Loading screen
services.description: Loads scenes in the background behind a loading screen with a progress bar and tips: Services.Get<GameLoader>().LoadScene("Gameplay").

services.name: Gameplay
services.description: The gameplay scene to build your game in: a HUD area and a pause menu (Resume, Settings, Main menu) that freezes the game.

services.name: Main menu
services.description: The first scene of the game: title and Play, Settings, Credits and Quit buttons wired to the services you added. Adds the Gameplay scene too.

services.name: Inputs
services.description: Keyboard, mouse and gamepad controls (move, look, jump, interact, sprint) and the Escape / Back key that closes menus and pauses: Services.Get<GameInput>().Move.

services.name: Controls
services.description: A screen where players change their keyboard and gamepad keys, saved for the next launch: Services.Get<ControlsScreen>().Open().

services.name: Responsive UI
services.description: Every ArchNet screen fits phones, tablets and computers, in portrait and landscape, away from notches. Click Update after adding screens.

services.name: Localization
services.description: Your game in several languages: English and French files with the texts of the ArchNet screens, translated labels, a Language choice in Settings, a key editor with CSV import / export.

services.name: Notifications
services.description: In-game notifications (info, success, warning, error) in a corner of the screen, a few at a time: Services.Get<GameNotifications>().Success("Saved").

services.name: API
services.description: Talk to your web API in one line: await Services.Get<GameApi>().Status(); one base URL per environment, timeout, retries, clear errors.
